blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Supply chain visibility, at the strategic level, is less a dashboard and more a decision engine. A company that truly sees its operation in real time is not just better informed; it is faster at every decision the day throws at it. The gap between seeing a problem at hour one and seeing it at hour twelve is not small — it is often the difference between a three-hour fix and a three-week recovery.

What is required to reach this level is rarely more software. It is cleaner data, better agreements with partners, and a cultural willingness to look at bad news early. Companies are often surprised to find that their investment gap is not technical at all; it is organisational.

Visibility, when done well, becomes an invisible but decisive edge. Competitors with the same physical assets and the same cost structures lose, over years, because they simply cannot see what the visibility-rich company sees — and therefore cannot act at the same speed.

items.q: At the strategic level, the text describes visibility as…
items.why: "is less a dashboard and more a decision engine" — visibilidade como motor de decisão, não painel.

items.q: According to the text, what is usually required to reach strategic visibility?
options: Cleaner data, better partner agreements and cultural willingness
items.why: "It is cleaner data, better agreements with partners, and a cultural willingness to look at bad news early."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Two rivals with identical assets can still perform very differently.
Seeing a problem early can shorten recovery dramatically.
The real barrier to visibility is often organisational, not technical.
Buying more software is the surest route to visibility.
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma que "what is required… is rarely more software" — logo, discordaria dessa ideia.

items.q: The phrase "a three-hour fix and a three-week recovery" is used to suggest that…
options: delays in seeing a problem compound its cost non-linearly
problems should be fixed within three hours
items.why: Inferência: o contraste mostra que enxergar tarde multiplica desproporcionalmente o custo do problema.

items.q: Why do rivals with the same assets and cost structures lose over the years?
options: They refuse to hire more staff
They cannot see what the visibility-rich company sees, so they act slower
items.why: "they simply cannot see what the visibility-rich company sees — and therefore cannot act at the same speed."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily apresentando o caso de investimento ao conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Let me start where it hurts. Twelve hours. That is how far behind our competitors were when the port went down — twelve hours ahead of us, not behind. They had rerouted, renegotiated and reassured their customers before we had even confirmed which containers were affected.

Now, I want to be careful here, because the instinct in this room will be to ask which platform we should buy. That is the wrong question. The systems we need are largely already licensed. What was missing that morning was not a screen; it was clean, shared data and a set of agreements with our carriers that were never actually signed.

So I am not asking you to approve a technology budget. I am asking you to approve a change in how we work. Bad news has to be surfaced early, and partners have to be trusted with data we currently guard. That is uncomfortable, and it is exactly why we keep losing the twelve hours.

If this is done properly, visibility stops being a cost line and becomes the edge that competitors with our very assets cannot copy.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How far ahead of the company were competitors when the port went down?
items.why: "Twelve hours ahead of us" — os concorrentes reagiram doze horas antes.

items.q: According to Emily, what was actually missing on the morning of the disruption?
options: Clean, shared data and signed agreements with carriers
items.why: "it was clean, shared data and a set of agreements with our carriers that were never actually signed."

items.q: What is Emily actually asking the board to approve?
options: A change in how the company works
items.why: "I am not asking you to approve a technology budget. I am asking you to approve a change in how we work."

items.q: When Emily says buying a platform is "the wrong question", she implies that…
options: the real gap is organisational, not a missing tool
the board should never invest in software
the existing systems must be replaced
items.why: Inferência: os sistemas já estão licenciados; o que falta é dado limpo, confiança e acordos — questão organizacional.

items.q: How would you best describe Emily's tone?
options: Candid and challenging, but with a clear proposal
items.why: Inferência: ela começa "where it hurts" e confronta o instinto do conselho, mas oferece um caminho concreto.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Real-time visibility turns the operation into a decision engine." A decision engine is…
options: a capability that converts information into faster decisions
items.why: Decision engine = motor de decisão: transforma o que se vê em decisões mais rápidas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The desk was better ___ than its rivals, and it moved hours earlier."
items.why: Informed = informado: quem enxerga em tempo real decide antes.

items.q: "The company faced a three-week recovery instead of a quick fix." Recovery here means…
options: the process of returning to normal operation
items.why: Recovery = recuperação: o tempo para voltar à normalidade após a ruptura.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Their real weakness was not the technology; it was the ___ between collecting data and actually using it."
items.why: Investment gap = lacuna de investimento: o vão entre coletar e usar o dado, onde o valor se perde.

items.q: "Done well, visibility becomes a decisive edge." A decisive edge is…
options: an advantage that determines who wins
items.why: Decisive edge = vantagem decisiva: o diferencial que define o vencedor ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre cadeia de suprimentos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the visibility programme." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the shared-data agreements carrier by carrier." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, etapa por etapa.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on sharing data with partners." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar em definitivo.

items.q: "The team agreed the plan but never followed through, so the agreements went unsigned." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Cleaner data and early warnings genuinely move the needle on recovery time." This means they…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir diferença perceptível.
